name: Mark Whalley
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: I work exclusively with adults, guided by three core principles: 1) “Meet the client where they are at.” 2) "The client needs an experience, rather than an explanation.” 3) “We are born in relationship, we are wounded in relationship, and we can be healed in relationship.” 1) Tailored, Collaborative Therapy Every client is unique, so I believe a ‘one-size-fits-all’ approach to therapy is inadequate. Instead, I practice Pluralistic Therapy, which allows us to co-create a therapeutic process that is tailored to the client’s individual needs. This integrative approach draws from a range of therapeutic modalities, including those listed below, and is informed by the latest research and theories in Intersubjectivity, Attachment, Trauma, Self-Compassion, and the Neuroscience of Psychotherapy. 2) The Power of Experience Over Explanation This principle builds on the first. However, when trauma, grief, or relationship challenges disrupt our inner narrative, that can create a sense of disconnection or overwhelm, often manifesting as anxiety, depression, or even somatic symptoms.

name: Carmel Nielsen
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: Carmel Nielsen is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA). Her professional expertise spans therapeutic counselling, advocacy, crisis intervention, program development, and the coordination of multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders. Carmel brings a deep commitment to inclusive, person-centred care and works with a broad scope of topics including emotion regulation, stress, motivation, trauma, self-concept, and workplace challenges.

name: Faye West
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: I work with children and adults, drawing on modalities such as Narrative Therapy, Expressive Therapies including Sandplay Therapy and Symbol Work, and using a play therapy approach with children. My particular areas of interest are disenfranchised and complex grief, identity/self-esteem, life transitions and parenting. I also provide supervision.

name: Vanessa Rohlf
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: Dr Vanessa Rohlf is a counsellor, consultant and educator specialising in supporting people who care for animals. She is an associate member of the Australian Psychological Society and has further qualifications in mindfulness and animal bereavement as well as certification as a compassion fatigue therapist with the Green Cross Academy of Traumatology. She provides collaborative, evidence-based, and compassionate support in several areas including pet loss, depression, anxiety, grief, burnout, stress, compassion fatigue, and trauma.

name: Cora Clough
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: Vedere Counselling, located in South Yarra, Melbourne, offers professional counselling services for individuals and couples facing challenges such as depression, anxiety, behavioural issues, relationship difficulties, substance abuse, stress, trauma, and grief. Led by registered clinical counsellor Cora Clough, the practice provides a safe, non-judgmental environment for clients to explore their thoughts and emotions. Cora's extensive background in social science and business enhances her therapeutic approach, fostering personal growth and resilience.

name: Lisa Lovell
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Clinical)
description: Lisa is a Registered Clinical Counsellor and Yoga teacher. She works with children and adults who have experienced major life stressors (life transitions, anxiety and stress, depression, grief and loss) and trauma that may impact their quality of life and relationships. She works from a process-oriented perspective, and is client focused and dynamic with her therapeutic modalities which includes integrative mindful movements to help release stressors from the body.

name: Nia K
title: Counsellor/Psychotherapist (PACFA Certified Practising)
description: Nia’s therapeutic practice is informed by her academic qualifications (Bachelor of Integrative Psychotherapy,Advanced Clinical Training in Relational Gestalt Psychotherapy,Graduate Certificate in Experiential & Creative Arts Practice,Advanced Diploma of Transpersonal Counselling) and life experience. She has a strong understanding of the connection between intergenerational trauma and the here and now experience of our lives. She explores what underlies many people’s experiences and the idea that trauma can be passed down from one generation to the next.
specialties: Posttraumatic stress disorder, Trauma recovery, Somatic psychotherapy
